title: Lesson 9: Communicating AI Wins (and Setbacks) Honestly
description: Communicating AI wins and setbacks honestly: what honest AI communication means, the two failure modes of overstatement (AI washing) and concealment, why accurate reporting is the durable trust strategy, and a reporting cadence that reports wins and losses with the same plain accuracy.

questions.question: Why does concealing a setback damage trust more than reporting it plainly?
options: Employees already use AI, so silence reads as withholding the whole story
Employees assume the setback was larger than it really was and overreact to it
Employees conclude the program has no setbacks and set their hopes too high
Employees stop asking questions because they believe the answer is already known
questions.explanation: Employees already know what AI can do, so a hidden setback reads as a leader holding back rather than as good news. Reporting wins and losses the same way is what makes later claims believable.

questions.question: A program reports that 40 percent of onboarding entries touched an AI draft while 11 percent were completed that way end to end. What is the honest way to report it?
options: Announce the 40 percent as adoption and describe the rest as in progress
Report both figures with their sources, separating reach from depth
Report only the 11 percent because it is the defensible number
Hold all reporting until the two figures can be blended into one
questions.explanation: Reach and depth measure different things, and presenting reach as finished work is the start of exaggeration. Naming each number and where it came from lets people follow up instead of doubting the claim.

questions.question: A strong result published months ago is still posted after the tool failed to scale. What is the right response?
options: Leave the old figure up because it was accurate when it was published
Remove the old figure quietly so that nobody notices the change
Revalidate published claims on a schedule and correct them openly
Withdraw every claim the program has made and start over
questions.explanation: Stale claims, more than new ones, cause most of the damage once conditions change. A scheduled review that revalidates or corrects published numbers keeps the record accurate at low cost.
